# Singapore start-up Ropedia raises US$22 mil in pre-Series A round for robot-training data The robotics data company has raised US$30 million so far, and will use the latest funds to gather more training data, increase device production and expand in Singapore and the US\. Ropedia, a Singapore start-up that supplies training data for robots and physical artificial intelligence systems, has raised US$22 million \($28\.4 million\) in a pre-Series A funding round\. It did not identify the investors in the latest round, saying only that it was led by venture firms with experience in AI, deep technology and infrastructure in Southeast Asia\. Ropedia's proprietary wearable devices record first-person video, depth, movement and audio as people carry out physical tasks\. # Naive raises $28\.5 million Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners **Business** Aug 06, 2026 Naive, a startup making business tasks easier with AI, just scored $28\.5 million in Series A funding led by Nexus Venture Partners \(with help from Y Combinator, Zetta, and some angels\)\. This bumps its total funding to $32 million\. ### Naive gains more than 30,000 developers Naive's platform lets you handle things like setting up US companies, email accounts, and cloud tools, all through one API\. More than 30,000 developers have jumped on board so far, boosting its revenue 10-fold into the low-double-digit millions\. CEO and co-founder Sean Dorje says the new cash will go toward hiring researchers and developing the company's four infrastructure projects: virtualized sandboxes for agents; model routing and inference optimization; a memory layer; and governance and orchestration\.
